study_families.study_label: 4-week incremental treadmill running training programme with weekly immune and urinary-proteomic monitoring (Guangzhou Sport University)
study_families.design: Single-arm, repeated-measures training-intervention study (no parallel control group); within-subject comparisons at pre-training baseline (W0) and after each of four weekly incremental training blocks (W1-W4). Not a single-bout acute pre/post design: each weekly timepoint follows a week of daily intermittent training, not one identifiable bout.
study_families.training_load: 4-week incremental treadmill running, intermittent mode, total daily running time 48-60 min, 5 d/week; weekly intensity W1=60%, W2=70%, W3=80%, W4=90% VO2max; weekly distance 39.73±2.69 (W1), 46.20±2.97 (W2), 42.16±2.49 (W3), 47.73±3.21 (W4) km
study_families.study_notes: Central timing ambiguity for this pilot item: the prose (Methods 2.3) states blood/urine were collected 'at the end of each training week' each Sunday morning, fasting, but does not state the exact time from the last training session to sample collection. Figure 1's timeline axis ('M T W T F 24h 48h') suggests training Mon-Fri with sampling ~48 h after the last (Friday) session, but this is inferred from a figure axis label, not stated in the Methods text -- flagged as UNCLEAR rather than assumed.

reports.title: Identification of Urinary Biomarkers for Exercise-Induced Immunosuppression by iTRAQ Proteomics
reports.authors: Xu G; Lin W; McAinch AJ; Yan X; Weng X
reports.reviewer_notes: Provisional view only (this is extraction, not a screening decision): best fit is 'background' per the v3 default for training snapshots with unknown last-bout timing (matches the pilot_purpose instruction to first calibrate as background pending clarification of the event-to-sample timing relationship). If an adjudicator treats each week's final session + the ~48h Sunday draw (inferred from Figure 1, not stated in text) as a known-timing bout, this could instead be scored as repeated acute challenges (B_support_repeated_bouts) across W1-W4, with W0 as baseline. This classification choice is the key unresolved question for this report.
reports.author_stated_use: Authors state the four ELISA-validated proteins (SEMG-1, PIP, PDGFRL, NDPK) 'may serve as noninvasive immune biomarkers for exercise-induced immunosuppression' and suggest they could help monitor athletes' immune status during training; they call for further validation in other populations (e.g. females, elite athletes) and with different training programmes, and state sensitivity/specificity of each biomarker still need to be tested.
author_window_interpretation_locator: p.2 Introduction: "the period of immunosuppression after high-intensity exercise is called 'open window' period [18]"
p.9 Discussion: "...we found that WBC counts, CD4+ lymphocytes, and CD4+/CD8+ ratio decreased...suggesting exercise-induced immunosuppression"

sample_sets.group_condition: single arm (all 15 participants pooled); no parallel control group
sample_sets.control: no separate control group; W0 pooled urine serves as comparator
sample_sets.matrix: urine (midstream, pooled across all 15 participants per timepoint)
sample_sets.assay_platform: iTRAQ 8-plex labeling + strong cation exchange + 2D LC-MS/MS; ProteinPilot 5.0 database search
sample_sets.repeated_sampling: yes; same 15 participants' urine pooled at each of W0-W4
sample_sets.pairing_structure: pooled composite sample per timepoint; no within-subject pairing possible at discovery stage
sample_sets.age_sex_stratum: all male, mean age 19.2±0.7 y (whole cohort, no substratum)
sample_sets.preanalytics: protease inhibitor cocktail (PMSF 1 mmol/L, Amresco) added to prevent proteolysis; samples placed in liquid nitrogen then stored at -80°C
sample_sets.normalization: ProteinPilot unused value ≥1.3; FDR-filtered; proteins with poor repeatability (|CV|≥0.5) removed; AVG≥1.5 = upregulated, AVG≤0.67 = downregulated
sample_sets.circadian: midstream urine collected alongside the fasting ~07:00 Sunday blood draw
sample_sets.sample_notes: Pooled discovery sample: "the urine samples collected from all the participants...were thawed and combined into one urine sample for each time point" (Methods 2.7). n=1 pooled sample per timepoint precludes any between-participant variance estimate at the discovery stage; the 2 values per timepoint are iTRAQ technical replicates, not biological replicates.

sample_sets.sample_notes: Central pilot focus for R42: Methods 2.10 states only that 'the protein content of SEMG-1, PIP, PDGFRL, and NDPK was tested according to the manufacturer's instructions of the ELISA test kits...using a Multiskan Spectrum' — it does not state whether this used the same pooled sample as the iTRAQ discovery or individual participant urine aliquots. Table 7 reports mean ± SD for W0-W4, which is compatible with either individual-level data (n presumably 15) or repeated reads of one pooled sample. Regardless of this, the ELISA validation is same-cohort / same-collection-round, i.e. NOT an independent cohort; no new participants were recruited for validation.

precision_validation.evidence_notes: Standard clinical haematology analyser (ADVIA 120) used per manufacturer instructions; no in-study CV/ICC/repeatability statistic reported for WBC/neutrophil counts. Granularity note: this row is scored at marker_family level (not per individual marker) for pilot practicality given the 24 named iTRAQ candidates share the same pooled-sample design; whether the formal validation-readiness map should instead be built per individual marker (e.g. SEMG-1 separately from PIP) is flagged in unresolved_questions.

Samples span W0 (pre_exercise_baseline) through W1-W4, but the exact time from the most recent training session to each weekly draw is UNCLEAR (see sample_sets); cannot confirm whether W1-W4 samples fall within the 0-72h organising window or represent recovery beyond it.
WBC and neutrophil counts are direct immune-cell counts, immune-specific by definition.

Repeated individual-level measurement across 5 within-subject timepoints exists (SD reported, n=15), but no ICC/CV/responder analysis or reference-change-value is reported; per manual guidance this is "observed individual-level change; natural variability/measurement error not quantified", not an individualised marker.

No infection/clinical-outcome follow-up or functional assay was conducted on WBC/neutrophil counts in this study; Discussion cites general URTI-risk literature but reports no study-specific clinical or functional linkage.
WBC/neutrophil/lymphocyte counts are established clinical assays, not novel candidates requiring independent validation in this paper.
Venous blood draw and standard automated haematology analysis; routine clinical feasibility, implicit rather than explicitly discussed by authors.

Flow cytometry (BD FACSCalibur) calibrated with CalibriteE 3-colour kit; standard protocol, but no in-study CV/ICC reported for CD4+/CD8+ measurement. Granularity note: this row is scored at marker_family level (not per individual marker) for pilot practicality given the 24 named iTRAQ candidates share the same pooled-sample design; whether the formal validation-readiness map should instead be built per individual marker (e.g. SEMG-1 separately from PIP) is flagged in unresolved_questions.
Same timing ambiguity as leukocyte_redistribution family: W1-W4 samples drawn 'at the end of each training week'; exact time from last session not stated.
CD4+/CD8+ T-lymphocyte subsets and their ratio are direct, immune-specific measures.
Within-subject repeated measures exist (Table 3, n=15) but no ICC/CV/responder-threshold analysis is reported.

CD4+/CD8+ changes are co-measured with the urinary-protein findings and interpreted narratively as 'immunosuppression', but no statistical association with a functional assay or clinical outcome is tested in this study.
Established clinical/research assay, not a novel candidate requiring independent validation here.
Routine flow-cytometry on venous blood; standard feasibility, not explicitly discussed by authors as a feasibility finding.

iTRAQ discovery used 2 technical replicates per pooled sample and removed proteins with poor repeatability (|CV|>=0.5) and FDR filtering (unused value>=1.3), i.e. an explicit technical-reliability QC step; however this assesses technical (not biological/individual) reliability because the discovery sample is pooled (n=1 per timepoint).

W0 is pre_exercise_baseline; W1-W4 urine pooled samples have UNCLEAR time-from-last-session (see sample_sets SS-R42-07..10); cannot place these weekly samples precisely within vs outside the 0-72h organising window from the text alone.

GO annotation of the 24 co-differential proteins shows 'immune system process' as the top biological-process category and small immune-relevant pathway hits (IgG binding: PIP, UMOD, IGLV3-21/4-69/2-18; complement: CD55), but most of the 24 named proteins (and the bulk of the 1854-protein universe) are general plasma/extracellular proteins without a demonstrated immune-specific role; specificity is annotation-based (GO/DAVID), not functionally confirmed.

Discovery-stage urine is pooled across all 15 participants into one sample per timepoint (n_biological_samples=1), which structurally precludes any between-participant variance/individualisation estimate at discovery. ELISA-validation individual-vs-pooled status is UNCLEAR (see SS-R42-11..15), so individualisation cannot be assessed for the validated proteins either.

Urinary protein changes are co-measured alongside the WBC/CD4/CD8 'immunosuppression' findings and interpreted via GO/STRING bioinformatics annotation, but no statistical association test, functional assay or clinical/infection outcome links the urinary proteins to immune function or illness in this study.

KEY FINDING for this pilot item: ELISA 'validation' of SEMG-1, PIP, PDGFRL and NDPK (Methods 2.10, Results 3.5, Table 7) reuses the SAME 15-participant cohort / same urine-collection round as the iTRAQ discovery (not an independent site or cohort); whether the ELISA assay itself was run on pooled or individual urine is additionally UNCLEAR (see SS-R42-11..15). Authors explicitly call for 'further studies...to validate the noninvasive biomarkers...in a different population' (p.10), confirming no independent-cohort validation was performed.
Authors explicitly frame urine as a noninvasive, easy-to-monitor matrix and state the 4 validated proteins 'are relatively easy to monitor' for athlete immune-status surveillance.

extraction_provenance.provenance_notes: Produced as the AI stand-in for reviewer B in the 10-report charting pilot (protocol v3.0, pilot dated 2026-10-05). Per PILOT_README.md and the design contract, this pilot's values, agreement rates and timings are NOT results and do not enter inclusion counts, the evidence map or the validation-readiness map.

eligibility_opinion.rationale: This is a 4-week incremental treadmill TRAINING study with weekly cumulative training blocks (not a single identifiable acute bout): blood/urine are drawn 'at the end of each training week' each Sunday (p.2, Methods 2.3), and the exact time from the last training session to that draw is never stated in prose (only inferable at ~48h from Figure 1's axis labels, which is not a textual definition). Per the manual's default ('training snapshots...with unknown last-bout timing' -> background) and the pilot_purpose's explicit instruction to calibrate this item as background pending clarification of the event-to-sample timing relationship, 'background' is the best-supported provisional tag; 'uncertain' is a defensible alternative and the timing ambiguity itself is this report's central calibration question (see unresolved_questions).

unresolved_questions: scope_stream boundary case (the report's designated pilot purpose): is a weekly cumulative training block with an ambiguous ~48h-inferred sampling delay (Figure 1 axis only, not stated in prose) enough to count as B_support_repeated_bouts (4 repeated 'bouts' = W1-W4) with baseline W0, or must it stay 'background'/'uncertain' because no single identifiable bout and no stated exercise_end_definition exist? This determines whether R42 ever reaches formal charting as A/B evidence.

Pooled discovery vs individual-level ELISA validation (the report's second designated focus): Methods 2.10 does not state whether the ELISA assay for SEMG-1/PIP/PDGFRL/NDPK (Table 7) was performed on the SAME pooled urine sample used for iTRAQ (n=1 per timepoint, in which case the mean±SD in Table 7 would need another explanation) or on individual participant aliquots (n~15). Either way it is same-cohort/same-collection-round validation, not an independent cohort -- but the manual's independent_validation_and_use domain and n_biological_samples/n_participants fields need a human decision on how to code genuinely unresolvable pooled-vs-individual ambiguity from an inaccessible-data paper.

Granularity of precision_validation: this file scores the 7 domains at marker_family level (leukocyte_redistribution, T_cell_subsets_or_function, proteome) rather than per individual named marker (e.g. SEMG-1 separately from the other 23 proteins), to keep the row count tractable; the validation-readiness map's intended unit of analysis ('per-marker') may require per-marker domain rows instead, especially for the 4 ELISA-validated proteins.

sample_role/time_bin controlled vocabulary gap: none of 'immediate_post'/'recovery_post'/'during_exercise' cleanly describes a sample taken after a week of repeated daily training blocks; 'other' or 'UNCLEAR' were the only non-guessing options used here, which may need a dedicated vocabulary value for weekly/periodic training-monitoring samples if such designs recur across the full corpus.

Whether the 24 named co-differential proteins (Tables 5-6) should be coded as 'named_immune_candidate' (post-hoc discovery, candidate_prespecification_status=posthoc_or_results_only) as done here, or whether an exploratory iTRAQ screen with a broad immune-biomarker aim effectively pre-specifies ALL annotatable proteins as candidates, changing candidate_selection_basis/candidate_prespecification_status coding guidance for untargeted omics discovery papers generally.

age_range/adult_stratum_separable confidence: only mean±SD age (19.2±0.7 y) is given, no explicit range; 'all_participants_adult' was used based on university-student context and informed-consent procedure, but this is an inference, not a stated range -- flagged as medium/low confidence.
